metaTitle: How to Improve Website & SaaS Conversion with UX | Designit
metaDescription: Improve website and SaaS conversion by finding where motivated visitors lose intent: separate traffic, offer and experience problems, then fix by impact.
h1: Improve conversion by fixing the experience, not the button colour
subtitle: When conversion is low, teams usually change what is easiest to change. We help you work out whether the problem is traffic, offer or experience, then fix the experience in order of impact.
author: Designit
aiAnswerTargets: How do I improve my website conversion rate?
Why is my SaaS trial-to-paid conversion low?
Is low conversion a traffic or UX problem?

cta.heading: Find the leak before you fix it
cta.body: Share your funnel and we'll tell you where we'd look first, and whether it's an experience problem at all.

sections.heading: What should you do first?
sections.answer: Find out whether low conversion is a traffic problem (the wrong people arrive), an offer problem (the right people don't want it at that price) or an experience problem (the right people want it and can't get through). Only the third is fixed by design.
body: Segment your funnel by source and intent before redesigning anything. If high-intent visitors convert poorly too, the experience is the likely culprit, and the biggest leak is usually at one specific step.

sections.heading: Traffic, offer or experience?
rows: Low engagement from all sources; visitors are not your buyers

items.title: Diagnose
items.body: Analytics, session recordings and heuristic review to locate and size each leak.

items.title: Prioritise
items.body: Rank leaks by business impact against effort.

items.title: Redesign the leaking steps
items.body: Landing pages, sign-up, onboarding or checkout, based on why people hesitate.

items.title: Validate and measure
items.body: Usability tests, then experiments or before-and-after measurement against the agreed metric.

faq.q: How do I know if low conversion is a UX problem?
faq.a: If high-intent visitors, such as people arriving from branded search or from a sales referral, also convert poorly, and drop-off concentrates at a specific step, the experience is the likely cause.

faq.q: What is usually the biggest leak?
faq.a: It differs by product. In e-commerce it is often checkout; in SaaS it is often the first session after sign-up; on B2B websites it is often an unclear first screen or a demo form that asks too much too early.

faq.q: Do we need a redesign to improve conversion?
faq.a: Usually not. Most gains come from fixing specific steps. A redesign is warranted when the structure itself is the problem.
